source_documents.title: Azulenes exhibiting solid-state fluorescence: synthesis and photophysics of 2-aryl-6-pyrrolidinylazulenes

reference_evidence_units.quote: Photophysical measurements revealed that fluorescence efficiency is primarily governed by the radiative rate constant, while the nonradiative rate remains relatively constant, indicating that activation of the radiative channel underlies the observed emission in the solid state.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 2a-2k
reference_evidence_units.statement: Across 2a-2k ΦFlu follows kr (0.6-1.5e7 s-1) while knr stays at 1.4-2.4e8 s-1.

reference_evidence_units.quote: This analysis suggests that the solid-state emissive behaviour of 2a–2k arises less from suppression of nonradiative decay and more from activation of the radiative channel in each derivative.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 2a-2k
reference_evidence_units.statement: Solid-state emission is switched on by the radiative channel, not by slower nonradiative decay.

reference_evidence_units.quote: These results indicate that the solid-state emission of 2a–2k can be rationalized by the formation of emissive H-type aggregates in the solid state, since the blue-shifted emission was also observed in the solid-state.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 2a-2k
reference_evidence_units.conditions: PMMA films of rising concentration, solid
reference_evidence_units.statement: Emission appears with concentration in PMMA and is assigned to emissive H-type aggregates.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Absorption does not change with concentration; no packing data.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The emission behaviour of 2a–2k should be explained by the steric constraints imposed by the two ester groups at the 1,3-positions, which restrict the rotation of the 2-aryl substituent, leading to a conformation orthogonal to the azulene ring.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 2a-2k
reference_evidence_units.statement: The 1,3-diesters lock the 2-aryl ring orthogonal to azulene.

reference_evidence_units.quote: By contrast, 3a–3k lacking the ester substituents, did not display emission behaviour, presumably because their 2-aryl substituents remain freely rotatable in solution.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 3a-3k
reference_evidence_units.statement: Without the esters the compounds are nonemissive, put down to free aryl rotation.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Hedged ('presumably'); no viscosity or low-temperature test on 3a.

reference_evidence_units.quote: These results support that the observed fluorescence most likely arises from a locally excited (LE) state rather than an ICT state.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 2a-2k
reference_evidence_units.statement: Small solvatochromism and azulene-localised orbitals: LE, not ICT, emission.

reference_evidence_units.quote: a clear transition from nonemissive to yellow fluorescence was observed in PMMA thin films as concentration increased [Fig. 5(c)]
reference_evidence_units.subject: 2a

reference_evidence_units.quote: kr values, also displayed higher FFlu (7.3%), indicating that increased radiative decay efficiency correlates with enhanced emission efficiency.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 2i
reference_evidence_units.statement: 2i has the largest kr (1.5e7 s-1) and the highest ΦFlu (7.3%).

reference_evidence_units.quote: This behaviour can be reasonably attributed to the suppression of thermally activated molecular motions at lower temperatures, which reduces nonradiative deactivation pathways and thereby enhances radiative fluorescence efficiency.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 2a
reference_evidence_units.statement: Cooling raises the emission of 2a in solution.

reference_mechanisms.label: RIM_RIR_RIV
reference_mechanisms.rationale: The esters restrict rotation of the 2-aryl group (orthogonal conformation), part of the paper's explanation next to the radiative-rate argument.

reference_mechanisms.label: AGGREGATE_EXCITON_EXCIMER
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Concentration-dependent turn-on in PMMA is assigned to emissive H-type aggregates; the paper adds that radiative decay becomes dominant in aggregates. Supporting explanation.

reference_mechanisms.label: RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE
reference_mechanisms.rationale: The abstract's explanation: ΦFlu across the series follows kr while knr stays nearly constant ('activation of the radiative channel'). 2i has the largest kr and ΦFlu.
